name: WA98
notes: Hall not identified: the experiment sat in the SPS West Area (WA designation; it used the Goliath magnet, which stood in the West Area until it moved to the North Area for NA57). The placement is the existing campus-level site:cern-meyrin (500 m precision), which is not a hall position, as for WA97.

WA98 followed WA80 and WA93 (section title of arXiv:2603.10835, 'Experiments WA80 to WA93 to WA98'; Specht slides: 'followed WA80'); WA80 and WA93 are not Atlas records, so no lineage row was written.
Approval: Greybook says 16 April 1992, the 2014 Specht slides say 1991; Greybook is used.
Spokespersons: Hans Gutbrod, then Terry Awes from 1997 (arXiv:2603.10835). No formation date or membership found.
INSPIRE experiment id not looked up: inspirehep.net is off-limits to coverage streams (STREAM_RULES); external.inspire_experiment left null for the integrator.

physics_goals.quote: The leap into a precision measurement of direct photons came with the WA98 experiment
physics_goals.value: Precision measurement of direct photons, neutral pions and charged-particle production in Pb-Pb collisions with photon and hadron spectrometers

summary.plain: WA98 was a CERN experiment in the SPS West Area that studied lead-lead collisions with a photon spectrometer, a hadron spectrometer and many global detectors. It made the first observation of direct photons in ultrarelativistic heavy-ion collisions and saw suppression of high-momentum neutral pions.
summary.technical: WA98: lead-glass photon spectrometer, two tracking spectrometer arms in the Goliath dipole (1.6 Tm) with time-of-flight, Plastic Ball, silicon drift and pad multiplicity detectors, a 21 m2 photon multiplicity detector, MIRAC and zero-degree calorimeters, on 158A GeV Pb beams, 1994-1996; direct photons at low pT, pi0 suppression, flow, DCC searches and photon interferometry; follow-up of WA80 and WA93.
